messages:
marie: Heads-up — CI canary flagged NaNs in attention outputs for long seqs (>2048) when ROPE+ALiBi are both enabled. Regression introduced in commit 8f3a2b (rotary scale tweak). Reproducer below and quick notes. :eyes:

marie: ```python
# repro snippet (simplified)
import torch
q = torch.randn(2, 8, 4096, 64, dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda')
k = q.clone()
# rotary apply (kernel changed in 8f3a2b)
q = apply_rope(q, scale=1.0)  # default changed in commit
scores = torch.einsum('b h t d, b h s d -> b h t s', q, k)
# NaNs show up after softmax for some batches
probs = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
```

ryan: I looked at the kernel diff. We promoted an intermediate multiply to fp16 to save memory. My hunch: when positions get large, sin/cos values times the fp16-quantized factors overflow/underflow and produce Inf which becomes NaN after softmax normalization.

anita: Adding to that — ALiBi injects a linear bias ~slope * pos. For long sequences the bias magnitude can dwarf the dot products. In fp16, exp(scores) overflows even if we subtract max, because intermediate exp still uses fp16 range.

josh: Two immediate mitigation ideas: (1) force accumulation/exp path to fp32 in the fused kernel, or (2) clamp the scores aggressively before exp. Note: simple max-subtraction (scores - max) is softmax-stable mathematically but not safe if exp is computed in fp16 and hits overflow.

marie: I reproduced that — casting scores to float32 before exp avoids Inf/NaN. So a minimal patch is: compute dot/rotary in fp16 for perf, but do `scores = scores.to(torch.float32)` before `torch.exp`/accumulation and then cast back.

sean: From an infra/runtime perspective we could also tweak the kernel selector: for fused ROPE+ALiBi, choose an accumulation dtype of fp32 when seq_len >= 1024 or when dtype==float16. We'll trade some latency for numeric safety.

dev-bot: Canary deploy kicked off for branch runtime/rotary-fix (build BR-2134). Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/BR-2134 :rotating_light:

anita: We should formalize this at the interface level: kernels should expose an `accum_dtype` flag in their kernel ABI so the runtime can select accumulation precision without modifying kernel source per model. Proposal: default to `auto` with hard thresholds (seq_len, dtype) and overrideable via model config. I'll draft an RFC.

ryan: Agreed. Also add unit tests that exercise ROPE-only, ALiBi-only, and ROPE+ALiBi combos across seq_len in {128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} and dtypes {fp16, bf16, fp32}. Add a numeric-regression guard that fails the build if token-level KL or max-abs-delta exceeds small thresholds.

marie: I'll open the RFC + a rollback PR that reverts the fp16 promotion and adds explicit accumulation casts in the fused kernel. Ticket INC-2147 created and linked in the PR. Running the canary now, will report back.

josh: If canary is green, plan: rollout to prod-sim group, monitor loss/latency for 24h, then full rollout. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:
